props.title: 8½
props.initialSlug: Life is the greatest circus of all

sections.content: 8½ (1963) revolutionized meta-cinema through Fellini's audacious exploration of creative crisis. The film follows Guido Anselmi, a director struggling to make his next film while wrestling with memories, fantasies, and relationships. Fellini's masterpiece influenced countless films about filmmaking, from All That Jazz (1979) to Adaptation (2002). The surreal blend of reality and imagination set new standards for non-linear storytelling, while Marcello Mastroianni's performance as Guido became the template for tortured artists on screen.

sections.content: The film's influence on depicting the creative process remains unmatched. Stardust Memories (1980) directly homages 8½'s style and structure, with Woody Allen channeling Mastroianni's existential crisis. Synecdoche, New York (2008) takes Fellini's meta-commentary to extreme levels, while Birdman (2014) echoes the blend of fantasy and reality in exploring artistic relevance.

The treatment of women in 8½ reflects both its era and Fellini's personal vision. The parade of females - from Guido's wife to his mistress to his fantasy figures - inspired later examinations of male gaze in cinema like Nine (2009), a direct musical adaptation, and Pain and Glory (2019), Almodóvar's more nuanced take on similar themes. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cinema

movies.title: The State of Things
movies.slug: Wenders' meditation on filmmaking and creative paralysis

sections.content: Contemporary filmmakers continue drawing from 8½'s well. I'm Thinking of Ending Things (2020) borrows its dream logic and nested realities. The Hand of God (2021) pays tribute to Fellini while examining artistic awakening. Even mainstream films like Inception (2010) owe a debt to 8½'s pioneering mix of memory, dream, and reality.
